items.title: Your Money - Your Data
items.text:
EuroKeep is a self-hosted personal finance management application that gives you full control over your financial data.

Unlike cloud-based solutions, EuroKeep can be deployed on your own infrastructure. Your accounts, balances, movements and budgets remain where they belong: under your control.

This documentation provides everything you need to deploy, configure and use your own EuroKeep instance.

items.title: What is EuroKeep?
items.text:
EuroKeep helps you manage your personal finances in a simple and privacy-focused way.

With EuroKeep you can:

  • Manage multiple accounts and currencies
  • Track income, expenses and transfers
  • Organize movements with categories
  • Create and monitor budgets
  • Analyze your monthly financial development
  • Hide sensitive information with Privacy Mode
  • Export monitoring information via Prometheus

The goal is not to replace complex banking software, but to provide a lightweight, transparent and self-hosted solution for managing your everyday finances.

items.title: Self-Hosted by Design
items.text:
EuroKeep is designed to run on your own server.

EuroKeep is delivered as a single Docker image, eurokeep/eurokeep, that contains the complete product:

  • Angular frontend
  • Nginx as web server
  • PHP-FPM application runtime

The only other service it needs is a MariaDB database. The provided Docker Compose file starts one for you.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
All you need is two files in an empty directory:

  • A Docker Compose file
  • An environment file (.env)

Database migrations run automatically on every start, and the default data is created on the first one.

After starting the containers, administrative tasks such as user creation and password management are performed directly inside the EuroKeep container using CakePHP CLI commands.

See Docker for the compose file and the environment file.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text:
A typical setup workflow:

  1. Put the compose file and the .env file into an empty directory
  2. Start the containers with docker compose up -d
  3. Put a TLS reverse proxy in front of port 8080 (login only works via HTTPS)
  4. Create your first EuroKeep user inside the EuroKeep container
  5. Configure accounts, categories and budgets
  6. Start tracking your finances

For detailed instructions, see the deployment and user management sections.

items.title: Account Management
items.text:
Create and manage your financial accounts, including:

  • Bank accounts
  • Cash accounts
  • Other balance sources
  • IBAN information
  • Multiple currencies

items.title: Money Tracking
items.text:
Record your financial activity through:

  • Income
  • Expenses
  • Transfers between accounts
  • Categories and comments
  • Automatic category suggestions based on previous bookings

items.title: Budget Management
items.text:
Budgets allow you to define spending limits for categories and their subcategories.

EuroKeep automatically summarizes matching movements and provides an overview of:

  • Current spending
  • Remaining budget
  • Exceeded limits
  • Related transactions

items.title: Privacy Mode
items.text:
Your financial information should remain private.

Privacy Mode allows you to hide sensitive information such as:

  • Account balances
  • Money movements
  • IBAN details

This makes it possible to safely use EuroKeep even when others can see your screen.

items.title: Monitoring
items.text:
EuroKeep includes an experimental Prometheus exporter for monitoring financial statistics.

⚠️ The exporter currently exposes sensitive information and should only be accessible to trusted systems.

items.title: Documentation Structure
items.text:
This documentation covers:

  • Deployment using Docker Compose
  • Container management
  • User administration
  • Account management
  • Money tracking
  • Transfers
  • Budgets
  • Monitoring
  • Application usage

items.title: The Philosophy Behind EuroKeep
items.text:
Your financial data is personal.

EuroKeep follows one simple principle:

Your Money - Your Data

No external service should decide where your financial information is stored.

By running EuroKeep yourself, you stay in control of your data, your infrastructure and your privacy.

items.title: Docker Environment
items.text:
This is the example environment file:

# Image version  
EUROKEEP_VERSION=rc

# Host port of the app. HTTP only.
# Not needed if you want to use the traefik drop-in.
EUROKEEP_PORT=8080

# Public address including https://. Required: without it the API refuses every request.
APP_FULL_BASE_URL=https://eurokeep.example.org

# Random value: openssl rand -hex 32
# NEVER change it after the first start.
SECURITY_SALT=

# Never true in production, it exposes stack traces.
DEBUG=false

ENABLE_REGISTRATION=false

# --- Standalone (standalone-*.yml): MariaDB database is created automatically on the first start.
DATABASE_NAME=eurokeep
DATABASE_USER=eurokeep
DATABASE_USER_PW=somesecretpassworddefinetelynotthisone

# --- Integrated (integrated-*.yml): your own database server.
#DATABASE_URL=mysql://eurokeep:<password>@<db-host>:3306/eurokeep?encoding=utf8mb4
# Existing Docker network through which <db-host> is reachable.
#DATABASE_NETWORK=mariadb-internal

# --- Development (*-development.yml): host directory for the nginx logs (access.log, error.log).
# Unset: no log files, nginx logs to stdout/stderr (docker compose logs).
#NGINX_LOG_DIR=/var/log/nginx

# --- Traefik (traefik.yml)
#EUROKEEP_DOMAIN=eurokeep.example.org
#TRAEFIK_NETWORK=docker-internal
#TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT=websecure
#TRAEFIK_CERTRESOLVER=letsencrypt

items.title: ENABLE_REGISTRATION
items.text: Always, ALWAYS set this to false unless you are creating a user or resetting a user's password right now. Never ever keep this set to true. If true, the login form shows the Create account button. Just specify a new user's username and password, click 'create account` and the new user is good to go. See User Creation

items.title: DEBUG
items.text: By default, set to false. When true, the EuroKeep application will respond with detailed error details, stacktraces, etc. If true, this could leak sensitive information, so better keep it set to false, unless you know, what you are doing.

items.title: DATABASE_NAME
items.text: The name of the database, that will be used.

items.title: DATABASE_USER
items.text: The username, the EuroKeep API uses to authenticate to the database.

items.title: DATABASE_USER_PW
items.text: The password, the EuroKeep API uses to authenticate to the database, combined with DATABASE_USER

items.title: DATABASE_URL
items.text: The User URL that lets EuroKeep API authenticate to your own database server.

items.title: DATABASE_NETWORK
items.text: If your own DATABASE_URL points to a docker network, you can configure that here.

items.title: NGINX_LOG_DIR
items.text: Host directory to put nginx logs (access and error). If removed, access logs will be put to stdout.

items.title: EUROKEEP_DOMAIN
items.text: The FQDN that points to your instance of EuroKeep.

items.title: TRAEFIK_NETWORK
items.text: If you use traefik with a virtual docker network, you can configure that here.

items.title: TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT
items.text: This is the entrypoint EuroKeep will be available on.

items.title: TRAEFIK_CERTRESOLVER
items.text: This is the certresolver for Traefik.

items.title: API Documentation
items.text: The API lives on https://apidocs.eurokeep.io/.

items.title: Running Commands
items.text:
Many management commands need to be executed in the EuroKeep container, since they are part of the CakePHP binaries.

The following command, run from your docker directory, opens a shell in the EuroKeep container. Here you can run the setup commands, e.g. create a new user.

docker compose exec eurokeep /bin/sh

items.title: User Manual
items.text: This manual is still under construction.

items.title: System Wide Features
items.text: There are multiple system wide features activated for EuroKeep.

items.title: Calendar Bar
items.text: Many views contain the calendar bar. That part lets you navigate from one month to another which affects the displayed time range.

items.title: Privacy Mode
items.text: If you click settings→hide data or show data, you can turn on an off the display of sensitive data. This applies to at least every balance object. No balance, whether an account balance nor transactions of money will then be shown. Also, the IBAN of your accounts will remain hidden until you click show data again.

items.title: User Management
items.text: User Management is only available through CLI.

items.title: Creating a User
items.text:
To create a user, log in to your environment’s CLI and execute the following command:

/var/www/html # bin/cake user_add
Add a new user.
Please enter email.
> mail@eurokeep.io
Please enter name.
> Mail
Please enter the password.
> Test
User #42, mail@eurokeep.io was created.
That's all, folks.

items.title: Resetting Password
items.text:
To reset an existing user’s password, execute the following command:

/var/www/html # bin/cake user_reset_password
Select the user of your EuroKeep instance, whose password will be reset.
1: Jan Nox (jan@nox.kiwi)
42: Mail (mail@eurokeep.io)
Please select a user ID (1/11) 
> 42
Please enter the new password.
> Test42!
The password of user #42, mail@eurokeep.io has been changed.
That's all, folks.

items.title: Removing a User
items.text:
Keep in mind, removing a user eradicates its existance. There will be no remains whatsoever, including accounts, transactions.

EVERYTHING will be deleted.

To delete a user from your EuroKeep instance, execute the following command:

/var/www/html # bin/cake user_delete
Select the user you want to remove from your EuroKeep instance
1: Jan Nox (jan@nox.kiwi)
42: Mail (mail@eurokeep.io)
Please select a user ID (1/11) 
> 42
Please enter the user email address for sake of security.
> mail@eurokeep.io
The user #42, mail@eurokeep.io has been deleted, including all accounts, transactions, etc.
That's all, folks.

items.title: Create an Account
items.text:
To create an account, click the plus icon in your account overview page or directly click here Create an account for your user.

At least, offer a name, an emoji and the account type and the currency the account is working with. Also, add the IBAN. For accounts without IBAN, this field will not be mandatory in the future, but it is for now.

After saving, you can click on the success message and directly go to your new account.

Otherwise, you can go to your account overview and find it there. there.

items.title: Modify an Account
items.text:
To modify an existing account, select the disired account in your account overview page and then click the pencil icon close to the account overview’s card in the top-right corner.

Then edit anything you want. Don’t forget to click the save icon when done.

items.title: Delete an Account
items.text:
Deleting an account is possible on the Account’s modification page. Select the disired account in your account overview page and then head to the modification area by clicking the pencil icon in the top-right corner.

On the left bottom area of the form, you can find the trashcan icon. Click that to remove the account.

Keep in mind, that deleting an account will automatically delete all transactions and transfers to that account. There will be no remains of the account whatsoever.

items.title: Create a Transaction
items.text:
In your account overview page, select the desired account. Click the plus icon in the top right corner.

Provide the comment, the spent balance and select the category for that transaction.

The category will be selected automatically, if you book a new transfer with the same comment.

During comment input, EuroKeep will try finding a previous booking entry with that commend.

Click the save icon

items.title: Modify a Transaction
items.text: In your account’s history, click on an existing transaction to open the transaction modification screen. Change the things you want and dont forget clicking the save icon.

items.title: Delete a Transaction
items.text: In your account’s history, click on an existing transaction to open the transaction modification screen. In the bottom left corner you can find the trashcan icon.

items.title: Transfering Money from one Account to Another
items.text:
Same as Booking Money. But if you select a Transfer Account before adding a new transaction, the negative value of your transfer will also be created for the selected Transfer Account.

However, when editing the transactions, you have to edit both transfers after another. This is not automated.

This behavior also applies to removing a transaction.

items.title: Budgets
items.text:
Budgets rely on the category management. A budget is a limited amount of money that can be spent for a category and it’s sub-categories.

This feature finds transactions of the current month that match the configured category and it’s sub-categories. These transactions will then be summarized into a value that was spent on the budget.

The transactions can be seen in your Budget Manager if you click a Budget.

The transactions of a budget are only filtered for the categories and the current month, making it possible to analyze a Budget accross multiple accounts which is pretty neat if you want to keep track of your money in terms of where you spend it.

Of course, it does not prevent you from spending money.

items.title: Creating a Budget
items.text:
Go to your Budget Manager and click the plus icon in the top-right corner.

Enter your title and your limit. Then select a category that should be used. Select the currency and the category your budget will limit.

items.title: Modifying a Budget
items.text:
Go to your Budget Manager and expand the desired budget by clicking it. Then you can see the pencil icon in the top-right corner of the budget’s card.

Change the fields as you desire, dont’t forget saving your changes afterwards.

items.title: Deleting a Budget
items.text:
Open the Budget modification form. In the bottom-left corner you can find the trashcan icon that will remove the budget.

Keep in mind: Deleting a Budget will not remove any other data from EuroKeep.

items.title: Visualizing Budgets
items.text:
Any Budget that you create will appear on the home screen of EuroKeep. This item will only show a progress bar for the budget. The bar represents the available amount. The shorter it gets, the less money is left for that budget.

Clicking on a budget here will bring you right to your Budget Manager and expand the Budget you just clicked. This reveals a more detailed view on that budget - It tells you the limit, the remaining amount or the exceeded amount. Also, it shows all transactions that were found in the current month that were used to build the amound of spent money. From here, you can e.g. edit a transaction directly.

items.title: Monitoring
items.text:
For now, EuroKeep has a very simple and dumb Prometheus exporter. This is under heavy development and it does not limitate the output whatsoever. Who has access to this controller, will be given all info on all budgets of all users. So handle with absolute caution!

PromQL Exporter

items.title: Summary
items.text:
For now, there is a simple way to build monthly overviews on your income and spending. You can configure that view to show one or multiple of your accounts. If you open your Summary, it will show you the opening and closing balance of your selected accounts. Also, you will be able to see all spendings and income chronologically. Now you can compare that month to the previous month by using the navigation bar on the page.

items.title: User Management
items.text: User Management is only available through CLI.

items.title: Creating a User
items.text:
There are two separate ways of creating users. The first one relies on your environment, the other one uses a native CakePHP Command.

To create a user through CLI, log in to your environment’s terminal and execute the following command:

/var/www/html # bin/cake user_add
Add a new user.
Please enter email.
> mail@eurokeep.io
Please enter name.
> Mail
Please enter the password.
> Test
User #42, mail@eurokeep.io was created.
That's all, folks.

items.title: Resetting Password
items.text:
To reset an existing user’s password, execute the following command:

/var/www/html # bin/cake user_reset_password
Select the user of your EuroKeep instance, whose password will be reset.
1: Jan Nox (jan@nox.kiwi)
42: Mail (mail@eurokeep.io)
Please select a user ID (1/11) 
> 42
Please enter the new password.
> Test42!
The password of user #42, mail@eurokeep.io has been changed.
That's all, folks.

items.title: Removing a User
items.text:
Keep in mind, removing a user eradicates its existance. There will be no remains whatsoever, including accounts, transactions.

EVERYTHING will be deleted.

To delete a user from your EuroKeep instance, execute the following command:

/var/www/html # bin/cake user_delete
Select the user you want to remove from your EuroKeep instance
1: Jan Nox (jan@nox.kiwi)
42: Mail (mail@eurokeep.io)
Please select a user ID (1/11) 
> 42
Please enter the user email address for sake of security.
> mail@eurokeep.io
The user #42, mail@eurokeep.io has been deleted, including all accounts, transactions, etc.
That's all, folks.

items.title: EuroKeep is Available For Docker
items.text: EuroKeep is available on docker hub. Create a directory to put the Environment file and the Compose File. Then run docker compose up and EuroKeep will be downloaded and started.

items.title: Compose File
items.text:
This file, as of October 21st 2026 is just an example, but it works. It tells docker to deploy two separate services: The EuroKeep application and a designated instance of mariadb.

services:
  eurokeep:
    image: eurokeep/eurokeep:${EUROKEEP_VERSION:-rc}
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: mysql://eurokeep:${DATABASE_USER_PW:?}@db:3306/eurokeep?encoding=utf8mb4
      SECURITY_SALT: ${SECURITY_SALT:?}
      APP_FULL_BASE_URL: ${APP_FULL_BASE_URL:?}
      ENABLE_REGISTRATION: ${ENABLE_REGISTRATION:-false}
      DEBUG: ${DEBUG:-false}
    volumes:
      - uploads:/var/www/html/uploads
      - logs:/var/www/html/logs
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy

  db:
    image: mariadb:11.8
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MARIADB_DATABASE: eurokeep
      MARIADB_USER: eurokeep
      MARIADB_PASSWORD: ${DATABASE_USER_PW:?}
      MARIADB_RANDOM_ROOT_PASSWORD: "1"
    volumes:
      - db:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "healthcheck.sh", "--connect", "--innodb_initialized"]
      interval: 10s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 30s

volumes:
  db:
  uploads:
  logs:

items.title: Environment File
items.text:
The environment file .env in your docker directory determines the most important settings. This one is much limited but it deploys a working instance of EuroKeep. For further information, please refer to the Docker Environment Documentation

APP_FULL_BASE_URL=https://eurokeep.my.example.domain
SECURITY_SALT=353d9d20b333fa9cd514e2e3cb7768ae9109f5as58e6bc128ecc783ff5c190cc          # openssl rand -hex 32  — never change it after the first start
DATABASE_USER_PW=Another0neBytesTheDu$t!
EUROKEEP_VERSION=rc
ENABLE_REGISTRATION=false
DEBUG=false

items.title: Running Commands
items.text:
Many management commands need to be executed in the EuroKeep container, since they are part of the CakePHP binaries.

Run them with docker compose exec from your docker directory. For example, this command creates a new user:

docker compose exec eurokeep bin/cake user_add
